title: Reunion Night
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC I — Old Friends, New Heat
paragraphs: Saturday began with Aarav being told to look at a woman properly.
Ananya Rao tapped the table once.
White shirt, top two buttons open because the AC was weak.
Sleeves rolled to the elbow, showing the clean line of her forearms.
Hair tied high, exposing the nape of her neck and the soft skin behind her ears.
Independent interview coach. Zero patience. And a body that still looked like it belonged in a much less professional room.
Ananya held his gaze longer than the exercise required.
Her eyes dropped once — not to his notes, but to the open collar of his shirt, the faint line of his throat, the way his Adam’s apple moved when he swallowed.
But the shift reached her mouth. The corner of it softened, then tightened again, as if she had almost allowed something she shouldn’t.
The school reunion began at seven.
The distance between those two events should have reset him.
By 6:40, Aarav stood in front of his mirror changing shirts for the second time.
He watched the way the black fabric stretched across his shoulders and chest. He thought about Ananya’s eyes dropping to his throat. He thought about whether Mira would notice the same thing.
“You asked which one makes shoulders look better.”
At the Kapoor house, Rhea’s elder sister Neha was already hosting.
Twenty-nine. Married. Comfortable in the way people became after years of knowing exactly where every plate lived.
Tonight she wore a soft cream blouse that sat low enough on her collarbones to make her look less like someone’s wife and more like someone who still remembered how to be looked at.
Her husband Arjun Rao stood beside the drinks table.
Thirty-one. Lawyer. Calm. Broad-shouldered in a way that made formal shirts look slightly strained across the chest.
Rhea called him “boring” because it irritated him.
He called her “child” because it irritated her more.
They had been doing this for four years.
Rhea came down the stairs in a fitted green dress.

The fabric clung to her hips and the soft curve of her ass before falling to mid-thigh. The neckline was open enough to show the clean line of her collarbones and the upper swell of her breasts when she moved.
His eyes moved once — slow, involuntary — from her face to the place where the dress tightened over her chest, then lower, to the bare skin of her thighs.
Rhea reached for a glass. The movement pulled the dress tighter across her breasts for half a second.
Neha laughed, but her eyes stayed on her husband’s face a beat too long.
Across town, Kabir reached his elder brother Rohan’s apartment to pick up a speaker.
Twenty-eight. Architect. Married to Rohan for three years.

She wore a black blouse, thin enough that the outline of her bra straps showed faintly when she moved, and loose trousers that sat low on her hips. Bare feet. One silver anklet that rested against the soft skin of her ankle.
Kabir noticed the anklet before the speaker.
Then the way the blouse shifted when she breathed.
Then the faint shadow between her breasts when she leaned against the doorframe.
Tara noticed where his eyes had gone.
Tara leaned over the table to unplug the speaker.
The movement made the blouse pull tight across her chest and the trousers dip lower at the small of her back, showing a thin strip of skin.
Kabir smiled, but his voice came out lower.
His thumb brushed the soft inside of her wrist.
She did not pull away immediately.
But the heat under Kabir’s skin did not leave with it.
At 7:15, the six finally occupied the same room.
Dark blue dress that sat close to her body, showing the narrow waist and the soft flare of her hips. Black shrug open at the front. Simple. Effective.
His eyes moved over her the way they had moved over Ananya earlier — throat, collarbones, the place where the dress stretched across her breasts when she breathed, the bare skin of her arms.
Short black dress that ended high on her thighs. Oversized shirt over it, unbuttoned low enough to show the clean line of her cleavage when she moved.
Dev had been checking the playlist.
His gaze dropped, just once, to the open shirt, the soft upper curves of her breasts, the way the short dress rode higher when she shifted her weight.
A second glance that lingered on the curve of her waist and the soft line of her neck.
Dev looked back at the screen.
Rhea’s dress had an open neckline that was still completely normal.
It still made Kabir’s mouth go dry when she turned and the fabric shifted against her breasts.
He behaved as if the ceiling was fascinating.
Old schoolmates. Partners. Spouses. Society friends.
Sana Qureshi arrived with her husband Mehul Suri.
Sana, twenty-seven. Event planner. Warm. Open. Married for two years.
Tonight her blouse sat close enough that the shape of her breasts was clear when she moved.
Mehul, twenty-nine. Product designer. Confident without needing volume.
His thumb brushed the soft skin of her wrist for half a second longer than necessary.
Later, Sana stood close to Aarav at the snack table.
Mira heard from three feet away.
But her eyes tracked the way Sana’s hand rested near Aarav’s forearm, the way her body angled toward him.
Across the room, Mehul asked Mira about her work.
It stayed on her mouth when she spoke, then dropped once to the open neckline of her dress, then returned to her eyes with complete control.
His glass stopped halfway to his mouth.
Kabir had forgotten they were invited.
Tara entered laughing at something Rohan said.
The black blouse still sat the same way. The anklet still caught the light when she walked.
She knew Tara. Had met her before.
She had never noticed Kabir noticing her like this.
Her hand rested at his back for one beat too long, fingers spreading slightly against the fabric of his shirt.
Nobody else saw the tiny current.
At the dining table, seating became its own game.
Every arrangement produced a second arrangement.
Who’s thigh almost touched whose when they shifted.
Jobs. Rent. Parents. School teachers. Bad haircuts.
Still, the tone never became neutral.
When Mira leaned toward Dev to show an old photo, their shoulders touched.
The soft side of her breast brushed his arm through the fabric.
When Arjun passed Rhea a bowl, their fingers brushed.
The contact lasted a second longer than needed.
Her smile stayed in place, but her eyes did not.
When Tara reached across Kabir for salt, her sleeve pulled back, showing the soft inner skin of her forearm and the delicate bones of her wrist.
Then higher, for half a second, at the place where her blouse gaped slightly when she stretched.
When Sana laughed and touched Aarav’s forearm, her fingers rested there long enough to feel the muscle under his skin.
Mira stopped chewing for half a second.
After dinner came old photos on the television.
Class ten. Bad uniforms. Awkward bodies.
The contrast with now became unavoidable.
A photo showed Mira and Aarav arguing at a science fair.
Aarav realized what he had said — the way the dress sat on her body, the way it made her look like something he was no longer allowed to look at for free.
Another photo showed Rhea asleep on a bus.
Rhea walked over to take it.
Close enough that she could smell his cologne and see the faint pulse at the base of his throat.
Close enough that if she leaned forward even slightly, her breasts would brush his chest.
Their hands overlapped around the cushion.
The heat that moved between their palms was not family.
Palm flat against the soft curve of her side, fingers spanning the place where her dress was thinnest, feeling the heat of her skin through the fabric.
Aarav’s thumb rested just under the edge of her ribcage.
Mira felt the exact pressure of every finger.
The place where his hand had been still felt warm.
Kabir was too busy arguing with Rhea.
Naina bent to pick up her dropped phone.
The short dress rode higher on the backs of her thighs.
Dev stepped back at the same time.
The soft press of her breast against his ribs through the open shirt.
His hand caught her upper arm, fingers wrapping around the warm skin.
Close enough to see the flecks in his eyes and the way his mouth had gone slightly open.
Near the balcony, Tara stood alone for a minute.
Her lipstick left a faint mark on the rim.
At the place her mouth had been.
Kabir stood there a second longer than he should have, glass still warm from her hand, the faint taste of her lipstick already in his head.
And nothing about it was neutral anymore.
Naina held eye contact a beat longer.
The marriage did not look fragile.
That made outside attraction more interesting.
Neha and Arjun stayed because it was their house.
Rhea went to the kitchen for water.
They stood alone for less than a minute.
Before she could answer, Neha entered.
At midnight, the core six moved to Kabir’s car and Mira’s cab.
Aarav ended up beside Mira in the back seat.
Naina leaned against the front seat talking to Dev.
Every red light felt too long.
At one turn, Mira’s knee touched Aarav’s.
At another, Rhea’s hand landed near Kabir’s gear hand.
By the time each reached home, nobody was thinking only about school.
Kabir remembered Tara drinking from his glass.
Rhea remembered Arjun admitting the look without admitting it.
And Kabir going still around Tara.
Dev remembered Naina against his chest for one second.
And Shalini’s instruction from the previous week:
Three tutors waiting in the week ahead.
The reunion had not created desire.
It had only made everybody easier to see.
